title: Introduction to Computerised Accounting
description: Class 11 Accountancy: need, components and advantages of computerised accounting; manual vs computerised accounting; accounting software like Tally; database concepts, GST and automation in accounting.

topics.title: Need, Components and Advantages of Computerised Accounting
topics.concept:
As businesses grow, the volume of transactions becomes too large to handle by hand. A Computerised Accounting System (CAS) uses computers and accounting software to record, process and report financial transactions. It applies exactly the same accounting principles you have learned — debit, credit, ledger, trial balance — but the computer does the posting, balancing and statement preparation automatically.

A CAS has four components, often summarised as people, procedures, data and machines:

  • Hardware — the physical machines (computer, server, printer, network).
  • Software — the accounting program (e.g. Tally) that processes the data.
  • People (operators) — the trained staff who enter and use the data.
  • Procedures & Data — the rules followed and the accounting information fed in.

The advantages over manual accounting are large:

  • Speed — thousands of entries processed in seconds.
  • Accuracy — once data is entered correctly, calculations are error-free.
  • Reliability & automatic reports — the trial balance, P&L and balance sheet are generated instantly and always agree.
  • Storage & retrieval — huge data kept in little space, found in moments.
  • Up-to-date information and easy scalability as the business grows.

There are also limitations — cost of setup and training, the risk of data loss or hacking, system failures, and reduced employment of clerks — but for any sizeable business the benefits clearly outweigh them.

examples.problem: Example 1: Name the four components of a computerised accounting system.
examples.solution:
People, machines, software, data.

  • Hardware, software, people (operators), and procedures/data.

examples.problem: Example 2: State two advantages of computerised over manual accounting.
examples.solution:
Speed and accuracy.

  • Greater speed (instant processing) and accuracy (error-free calculations).
examples.answer: Greater speed and accuracy (also automatic reports, easy storage and retrieval).

examples.problem: Example 3: Give one limitation of computerised accounting.
examples.solution:
Risk/cost.

  • Risk of data loss or hacking (also high setup cost, training needs, system failure).
examples.answer: Risk of data loss/hacking (or high cost of setup and training, or system failure).

recap:
• CAS applies the same accounting rules but the computer posts, balances and reports automatically.
  • Components: hardware, software, people, procedures/data.
  • Advantages: speed, accuracy, automatic reliable reports, storage/retrieval, scalability. Limits: cost, data loss/hacking, system failure.

options: The same accounting principles as manual
quiz.explanation: The principles are the same; only the processing is automated.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a component of a CAS?
quiz.explanation: The components are hardware, software, people and procedures/data.

topics.title: Manual vs Computerised Accounting and Accounting Software
topics.concept:
Both systems reach the same destination — final accounts — but the journey differs.

BasisManual accountingComputerised accounting
Recordingby hand in booksdata entered once into software
Posting & balancingdone manuallydone automatically
Trial balance & reportsprepared manually, may not tallygenerated instantly, always tally
Speed & accuracyslow, error-pronefast, accurate
Backupphysical copies onlyelectronic backups possible

In a CAS, the user does the identifying and recording (entering vouchers); the software does the classifying, summarising and reporting. This is why correct data entry is so important — "garbage in, garbage out."

Accounting software comes in three broad kinds:

  • Ready-to-use (packaged) software — standard, low-cost packages for small/medium firms (e.g. Tally, Busy). Easy to learn but less customisable.
  • Customised software — a ready package modified to suit a firm's special needs; costs more.
  • Tailor-made (bespoke) software — built specially for a large organisation's unique requirements; most expensive, needs trained staff.

In India, Tally (and now Tally Prime) is the most widely used package — it handles vouchers, ledgers, inventory, GST, payroll and instant final accounts. Learning its concepts (creating a company, ledgers, voucher entry) is a valuable, employable skill that builds directly on this course.

examples.solution:
User enters; software posts.

  • The user records (enters) the data; the software posts, balances and reports automatically.
examples.answer: The user records the data; the software does the posting, balancing and reporting.

examples.problem: Example 2: Name the three kinds of accounting software.
Example 3: Which accounting package is most widely used in India?
examples.solution:
A household name.

quiz.q: In a computerised system, the trial balance is:
quiz.explanation: The software generates a tallied trial balance automatically.

quiz.q: Low-cost standard packages for small firms are ____ software.
quiz.explanation: Ready-to-use (packaged) software like Tally suits small/medium firms.

topics.title: Database Concepts, GST and Automation in Accounting
topics.concept:
At the heart of every accounting package is a database — an organised collection of related data stored so it can be easily accessed and managed. Some basic database terms:

  • Data — raw facts (e.g. a customer's name, an amount).
  • Field — a single item of data (a column, e.g. "Invoice No.").
  • Record — a complete set of fields about one entity (a whole row, e.g. one invoice).
  • Table — a collection of related records.
  • Primary key — a field that uniquely identifies each record (e.g. account code).

Accounting software stores ledgers, vouchers and inventory in such tables, linked together, so a single voucher automatically updates the ledger, the trial balance and the final accounts — one entry, many updates. This is the power of a database-driven system.

Modern packages are also GST-ready. When you enter a sales voucher, the software automatically computes CGST + SGST (intra-state) or IGST (inter-state), records the output tax, tracks input tax credit on purchases, and can even generate the GST returns — a task that would take hours by hand.

This automation is the real meaning of computerised accounting: the accountant focuses on judgement (what to record, how to classify, how to interpret) while the machine handles the mechanics (posting, totalling, tax, reports) instantly and without error. Knowing both the principles (from this whole course) and the tools (software, databases, GST) makes you ready for the real world — and for Class 12, CUET, B.Com and CA Foundation, where these foundations are built upon. That completes Class 11 Accountancy: from the very first transaction to a fully computerised, tax-compliant set of books.

examples.problem: Example 1: In a database, what is a 'record'?
examples.solution:
A full row.

  • A record is a complete set of fields about one entity (one whole row, e.g. one invoice).
examples.answer: A complete set of related fields about one entity — one full row in a table.

examples.solution:
Unique identifier.

  • It uniquely identifies each record in a table (e.g. account code).
examples.answer: It uniquely identifies each record in a table (no two records share the same primary key).

examples.problem: Example 3: How does GST-ready software help on a sales voucher?
examples.solution:
Auto-tax.

  • It automatically computes CGST+SGST or IGST, records the tax, and tracks input credit.
examples.answer: It automatically computes and records the correct GST (CGST+SGST or IGST) and tracks input tax credit.

recap:
• Database terms: data → field (column) → record (row) → table; primary key uniquely identifies a record.
  • One voucher auto-updates ledger, trial balance and final accounts (database-driven).
  • GST-ready software auto-computes CGST/SGST/IGST and tracks input tax credit; automation handles the mechanics while the accountant exercises judgement.

quiz.q: A field that uniquely identifies each record is the:
quiz.explanation: The primary key uniquely identifies each record.

quiz.q: On an intra-state sales voucher, GST-ready software computes:
quiz.explanation: Intra-state supplies attract CGST + SGST, computed automatically.

questions.q: A computerised accounting system uses ____ accounting principles as manual.
questions.explanation: The principles are identical; only processing is automated.

questions.q: Which is a component of a CAS?
questions.explanation: Components: hardware, software, people, procedures/data.

questions.q: The physical machines in a CAS are the:
questions.explanation: Hardware = the physical machines.

questions.q: An advantage of computerised accounting is:
questions.explanation: Speed and accuracy are key advantages.

questions.q: A limitation of computerised accounting is:
questions.explanation: Data loss/hacking (and cost, system failure) are limitations.

questions.q: In a CAS, posting and balancing are done:
questions.explanation: The software posts and balances automatically.

questions.q: Standard low-cost packages for small firms are ____ software.
questions.explanation: Ready-to-use packaged software (e.g. Tally).

questions.q: The most widely used accounting package in India is:
questions.explanation: Tally (Tally Prime) is the most widely used in India.

questions.q: Software built specially for one large organisation is ____ software.
questions.explanation: Bespoke/tailor-made software is built for unique needs.

questions.q: An organised collection of related data is a:
questions.explanation: A database is an organised collection of related data.

questions.q: A single item of data (a column) is a:
questions.explanation: A field is a single data item (a column).

questions.q: A complete set of fields about one entity (a row) is a:
questions.explanation: A record is a full row about one entity.

questions.q: A field that uniquely identifies each record is the:
questions.explanation: The primary key uniquely identifies each record.

questions.q: On an inter-state sale, GST-ready software computes:
questions.explanation: Inter-state supplies attract IGST.

questions.q: 'Garbage in, garbage out' warns that a CAS depends on:
questions.explanation: Reliable output requires accurate data entry.

questions.q: A firm enters one sales voucher and finds its ledger, trial balance and balance sheet all updated at once. This is because the software is:
options: Database-driven, so linked tables update from a single entry
questions.explanation: Linked database tables let one voucher automatically update every related report.

questions.q: Why is correct data entry MORE critical in a CAS than the arithmetic itself?
options: The software's calculations are error-free, so wrong input is the main risk ('garbage in, garbage out')
questions.explanation: Computation is reliable; the weak link is the human-entered data, so accuracy of input governs output quality.

questions.q: A fast-growing firm needs special features no package offers. The best choice is:
questions.explanation: Unique requirements at scale justify bespoke software built for the organisation, despite higher cost.

questions.q: Goods sold intra-state for Rs 1,00,000 at 18% GST: the software records output tax of:
questions.explanation: Intra-state 18% splits into CGST 9% (9,000) and SGST 9% (9,000), total 18,000 output tax.

questions.q: The chief role left to the human accountant in an automated system is:
options: Judgement — what to record, how to classify and interpret
questions.explanation: Machines handle the mechanics; humans supply the judgement the software cannot.

questions.q: In a database table of invoices, 'Invoice No.' that is unique for every invoice serves as the:
questions.explanation: A field that uniquely identifies each record is the primary key.

questions.q: A manual trial balance may fail to tally, but a computerised one always tallies because:
options: The software enforces equal debits and credits on every posting
It never makes errors of principle
questions.explanation: Automatic double-entry posting keeps debits equal to credits, so the generated trial balance tallies (though errors of principle can still exist).

questions.q: Which limitation of a CAS is a genuine risk that manual systems largely avoid?
options: Loss of data through system crash or hacking
questions.explanation: Electronic data is exposed to crashes and cyber-attacks, a risk paper records do not share.

questions.q: Input tax credit tracked by GST software lets a firm:
options: Reduce its GST payable by the GST already paid on purchases
questions.explanation: Input tax credit offsets output GST with the GST paid on inputs, lowering the net tax payable.

questions.q: Learning Tally builds directly on this course because the software still uses:
options: Ledgers, vouchers, debit/credit and final accounts
questions.explanation: Tally automates the very concepts learned here — ledgers, vouchers, double entry and final accounts.
